turn_0002.0: ❤️ The human heart – let's learn it simply!
turn_0002.1: The human heart is one of the most important organs in our body. It acts like a natural blood pump.
turn_0002.2: Let's learn about the heart step by step, starting with the basics.
turn_0002.3: Lesson 1: Where is the heart located?
turn_0002.19: The heart is located near the center of our chest, slightly to the left.
turn_0002.20: It is approximately the size of our fist.
turn_0002.24: An adult heart usually weighs 250–350 grams.
turn_0002.28: At rest, an adult heart generally beats 60–100 times per minute.
turn_0002.33: Lesson 2: The four chambers of the heart
turn_0002.49: The human heart has four chambers.
turn_0002.54: Receives oxygen-poor blood returning from the body
turn_0002.60: Receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs
turn_0002.67: Important point: The muscular wall of the left ventricle is thick because it must pump blood under pressure throughout the body.
turn_0002.100: This cycle continues throughout our lives.
turn_0002.101: Lesson 4: Why does the heart beat?
turn_0002.102: The contraction and relaxation of the heart muscles produce the heartbeat.
turn_0002.103: Systole (contraction): The heart contracts and pumps blood out.
turn_0002.107: Diastole (relaxation): The heart relaxes and fills with blood again.
turn_0002.112: The heart's natural electrical conduction system coordinates these beats. Its main starting point is called the SA node.
turn_0002.113: Lesson 5: How can we keep the heart healthy?
turn_0002.114: Daily walking, a diet rich in vegetables and fruit, enough sleep, avoiding tobacco, and controlling blood pressure help keep the heart healthy.

turn_0003.0: Do all the valves open at the same time?

turn_0004.0: No. ❤️ The heart's four valves do not all open at the same time. During different stages of the heartbeat, when two valves are open, the other two are closed.
turn_0004.1: There are four valves in the heart:
turn_0004.2: Tricuspid valve – between the right atrium and right ventricle.
turn_0004.6: Mitral valve – between the left atrium and left ventricle.
turn_0004.10: Pulmonary valve – between the right ventricle and pulmonary artery.
turn_0004.14: Aortic valve – between the left ventricle and aorta.
turn_0004.43: Systole – when the ventricles pump blood out
turn_0004.49: An important point: There are also brief phases of the heartbeat when all four valves are closed. But all four never open at the same time.
turn_0004.50: This is because blood must flow in only one direction. The valves prevent blood from flowing backward.

turn_0006.0: Yes, blood is purified in the body. But ❤️ the heart does not purify blood directly. The heart's main job is to pump blood throughout the body.
turn_0006.1: Three main organs are involved in cleaning the blood and maintaining its quality.
turn_0006.17: They remove carbon dioxide from the blood and add oxygen to it.
turn_0006.36: They filter waste products such as urea, along with excess water and salts, from the blood and excrete them as urine.
turn_0006.55: It processes medicines and some toxins and helps remove them from the body.
turn_0006.59: ❤️ What is the connection between the heart and lungs?
turn_0006.60: Oxygen-poor blood from the body reaches the right side of the heart.
turn_0006.64: The heart sends that blood to the lungs.
turn_0006.68: In the lungs, carbon dioxide is removed and oxygen is added.
turn_0006.72: Oxygen-rich blood returns to the left side of the heart.
turn_0006.76: The heart sends it throughout the body again.
turn_0006.90: Kidneys – filter waste from the blood.
